sections.title: Reading — an advertisement and the customers' comments

exercises.instructionEn: Read the advertisement and fill in the gaps with adjectives from the list below.
exercises.instructionUz: Reklamani o'qing va bo'shliqlarni quyidagi ro'yxatdagi sifatlar bilan to'ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
RO'YXAT: home-made, busy, reasonable, tasty, helpful,
         rich, perfect

REKLAMA (to'ldirilgan holda):

  Luigi's is the new Italian restaurant on Compton Street.
  It's open for lunch and dinner every day.
  There are many TASTY pizzas and delicious pasta dishes to
  choose from. Try the Special Spaghetti with RICH garlic
  sauce and of course the HOME-MADE garlic bread!
  The waiters here are always very HELPFUL and the prices
  are quite REASONABLE. Two people can eat at Luigi's for
  only £10. It is open from eleven in the morning till ten
  in the evening.
  Luigi's is the PERFECT place to enjoy a meal with friends.
  However, make sure you book first because it is always
  very BUSY in the evenings.

O'ZBEKCHA TARJIMASI:
  'Luigi's' — Compton ko'chasidagi yangi italyan restorani.
  U har kuni tushlik va kechki ovqat uchun ochiq.
  Tanlash uchun ko'p MAZALI pitsalar va mazali makaron
  taomlari bor. QUYUQ sarimsoqli sousli maxsus spagettini
  va, albatta, UYDA PIShIRILGAN sarimsoqli nonni tatib
  ko'ring!
  Bu yerdagi ofitsiantlar doim juda YORDAMCHAN, narxlar
  esa ancha O'RTACHA. Ikki kishi 'Luigi's' da atigi 10 funtga
  ovqatlanishi mumkin. U ertalab soat 11 dan kechqurun soat
  10 gacha ochiq.
  'Luigi's' — do'stlar bilan ovqatlanish uchun MUKAMMAL joy.
  Ammo, avval stol band qilishga ishonch hosil qiling, chunki
  kechqurunlari u doim juda GAVJUM bo'ladi.

YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  reasonable = o'rtacha (narx haqida — qimmat emas)
  perfect = mukammal, eng yaxshi
  make sure = ishonch hosil qilmoq

items.textEn: There are many 1) ............ pizzas and delicious pasta dishes to choose from.
items.whyUz:
'tasty pizzas' = mazali pitsalar.
taste (ta'm) + -y = mazali.
Coursebook 55-betda ham 'tasty dishes' bor edi.

items.textEn: Try the Special Spaghetti with 2) ............ garlic sauce ...
items.whyUz:
'rich sauce' = quyuq, to'yimli sous.
DIQQAT: 'rich' bu yerda 'boy' emas, 'quyuq' ma'nosida.
Coursebook 55-betda ham 'pasta with rich tomato sauce' bor edi.

items.textEn: ... and of course the 3) ............ garlic bread!
items.whyUz:
'home-made garlic bread' = uyda pishirilgan sarimsoqli non.
Coursebook 55-betda ham 'home-made bread' bor edi.

items.textEn: The waiters here are always very 4) ............
items.whyUz:
'helpful waiters' = yordamchan ofitsiantlar.
help + -ful.
Coursebook 55-betda ham bor edi.

'reasonable prices' = o'rtacha (maqbul) narxlar — qimmat emas.
Keyingi gap buni tasdiqlaydi: 'Two people can eat for only £10.'
Aksi: expensive (qimmat).

items.textEn: Luigi's is the 6) ............ place to enjoy a meal with friends.
items.whyUz:
'the perfect place' = mukammal joy.
'the' bilan keladi, chunki eng yuqori daraja.

items.textEn: ... because it is always very 7) ............ in the evenings.
items.whyUz:
'very busy' = juda gavjum.
Shuning uchun oldindan stol band qilish kerak.
Coursebook 55-betda ham 'it is very busy, so don't forget to book' bor edi.
Talaffuz: /ˈbɪzi/ — 'bizi'.

exercises.instructionEn: Read the people's comments and fill in the gaps with words from the list below.
exercises.instructionUz: Odamlarning fikrlarini o'qing va bo'shliqlarni quyidagi ro'yxatdagi so'zlar bilan to'ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
RO'YXAT: expensive, hard, empty, horrible, terrible,
         cold, rude

BU FIKRLAR REKLAMAGA TESKARI!
Har bir mijoz reklamada maqtalgan narsani TANQID qiladi.

Har bir bo'shliqning BIRINCHI HARFI berilgan —
shunga qarab so'zni topish oson.

YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  horrible = dahshatli, juda yomon
  hard = qattiq (non haqida — eskirgan)
  rude = qo'pol (aksi: polite)
  expensive = qimmat (aksi: cheap)
  terrible = dahshatli, juda yomon
  empty = bo'sh (aksi: full, busy)

items.whyUz:
'The food is HORRIBLE!' = Ovqat dahshatli!
REKLAMADA: 'tasty pizzas and delicious pasta dishes'.
Mijoz TESKARI aytyapti.

items.textEn: 2  The garlic bread is very h............ ! I think it's about three days old!
items.whyUz:
'very HARD' = juda qattiq (non eskirgan).
Keyingi gap buni tushuntiradi: 'about three days old'.
REKLAMADA: 'home-made garlic bread' (yangi pishirilgan).

items.textEn: 3  I don't like this spaghetti — it's c............ .
items.whyUz:
'it's COLD' = u sovuq.
Issiq taom sovuq bo'lsa — bu jiddiy kamchilik.
REKLAMADA: 'Special Spaghetti with rich garlic sauce'.

'very RUDE' = juda qo'pol.
REKLAMADA: 'The waiters are always very helpful'.
'rude' — 'polite' (odobli) ning aksi.

items.textEn: 5  It's a very e............ restaurant — this tiny pizza costs £5!
items.whyUz:
'very EXPENSIVE' = juda qimmat.
Keyingi gap buni tasdiqlaydi: 'this tiny pizza costs £5'.
REKLAMADA: 'the prices are quite reasonable'.
'tiny' = juda kichkina.

items.textEn: 6  It's a t............ place for a meal with friends! We're leaving now!
items.whyUz:
'a TERRIBLE place' = dahshatli joy.
REKLAMADA: 'the perfect place to enjoy a meal with friends'.
'We're leaving now' = biz hozir ketyapmiz.

items.textEn: 7  You don't need to book a table! Look — it's nearly e............ .
items.whyUz:
'nearly EMPTY' = deyarli bo'sh.
REKLAMADA: 'it is always very busy in the evenings'.
'nearly' = deyarli.

exercises.instructionEn: Do the people agree with the advertisement above?
exercises.explanationUz:
REKLAMA va MIJOZLAR FIKRINI SOLIShTIRING:

  REKLAMA                    MIJOZLAR
  tasty pizzas          ↔  The food is horrible.
  home-made bread       ↔  The bread is hard (3 days old).
  Special Spaghetti     ↔  The spaghetti is cold.
  helpful waiters       ↔  The waiters are rude.
  reasonable prices     ↔  It's very expensive (£5 a pizza).
  the perfect place     ↔  It's a terrible place.
  always very busy      ↔  It's nearly empty.

HAR BIR NUQTA BO'YICHA TESKARI!

items.textEn: Do the people agree with the advertisement?
items.answer: No, they don't. They say the opposite of everything in the advertisement.
items.whyUz:
Mijozlar reklamadagi HAR BIR gapni rad etadi.
'to agree with' = rozi bo'lmoq;
'the opposite' = teskari, aksi.
Demak, reklama HAQIQATNI aks ettirmaydi.

exercises.instructionEn: Write C for countable or U for uncountable.
exercises.instructionUz: Sanaladigan uchun C, sanalmaydigan uchun U yozing.
exercises.explanationUz:
C = countable (sanaladigan)
U = uncountable (sanalmaydigan)

TEKSHIRISH: otning oldiga son qo'yib ko'ring.
  'two olives' — mumkin → C
  'two sugars' — odatda mumkin emas → U

KITOBDA BERILGAN: 1 = U (ham).

items.whyUz:
Kitobda BERILGAN javob: U.
Massa — sanab bo'lmaydi.
Sanash uchun: 'a slice of ham'.

SANALADIGAN — 'an olive, two olives'.
DIQQAT: 'olive oil' (zaytun moyi) esa SANALMAYDI.

SANALMAYDIGAN — kukun.
'a sugar' XATO.
SANALADIGAN — 'a pear, two pears'.

SANALMAYDIGAN — suyuqlik.
Sanash uchun: 'a carton of milk'.
SANALADIGAN — 'a potato, two potatoES' (-o → -ES).

SANALMAYDIGAN — kukun.
Sanash uchun: 'a packet of flour'.
SANALMAYDIGAN — massa.
SANALMAYDIGAN — quyuq suyuqlik.

SANALADIGAN — 'a steak, two steaks'.
'a steak' = go'shtning bir kesilgan bo'lagi (porsiya).
DIQQAT: 'meat' esa SANALMAYDI.
Talaffuz: /steɪk/.

SANALMAYDIGAN.
Sanash uchun: 'a loaf of bread', 'a slice of bread'.
SANALADIGAN — 'an egg, two eggs'.
SANALADIGAN — 'an apple, two apples'.

SANALMAYDIGAN — suyuqlik.
Sanash uchun: 'a cup of coffee'.

exercises.instructionEn: Mrs Hardy is at the supermarket. Look at her shopping list and complete it with these words.
exercises.instructionUz: Xardi xonim supermarketda. Uning xarid ro'yxatiga qarang va uni quyidagi so'zlar bilan to'ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
SO'ZLAR: bottles, cartons, kilos, loaves, packets, slices

HAMMASI KO'PLIKDA berilgan, chunki ro'yxatda
sonlar 2 dan katta.

XARID RO'YXATI (to'ldirilgan holda):
  2 BOTTLES of wine        6 eggs
  3 KILOS of potatoes      2 lettuces
  2 CARTONS of milk        12 sausages
  12 SLICES of salami      2 frozen pizzas
  2 LOAVES of bread        5 bananas
  4 PACKETS of flour       6 oranges

DIQQAT — O'NG USTUNDA MIQDOR SO'ZI YO'Q:
  'eggs', 'lettuces', 'sausages', 'pizzas', 'bananas',
  'oranges' — SANALADIGAN otlar, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri
  son bilan sanaladi.

QAYSI SO'Z QAYSI OT BILAN:
  bottles → suyuqlik (wine)
  cartons → qog'oz paketdagi suyuqlik (milk)
  kilos   → og'irlik bilan (potatoes)
  loaves  → FAQAT non (bread)
  packets → quruq kukun (flour)
  slices  → yupqa kesiladigan (salami)

YANGI SO'Z:
  salami = salyami (dudlangan kolbasa)
  frozen = muzlatilgan

items.whyUz:
'2 bottles of wine' = ikki shisha vino.
Vino DOIM shishada sotiladi.

'3 kilos of potatoes' = uch kilo kartoshka.
Kartoshka og'irlik bilan sotiladi.
DIQQAT: 'potatoes' — KO'PLIKDA.

'2 cartons of milk' = ikki paket sut.
'a carton' — qog'ozdan yasalgan to'rtburchak idish.

'12 slices of salami' = o'n ikki bo'lak salyami.
Salyami YUPQA kesib beriladi.

'2 loaves of bread' = ikki (butun) non.
'loaf' → 'LOAVES' (-f → -VES).
DIQQAT: 'loaf' FAQAT non uchun ishlatiladi.

'4 packets of flour' = to'rt paket un.
Quruq kukun mahsulotlar paketda sotiladi.

exercises.instructionEn: Choose the correct words to complete this dialogue between Mrs Hardy and a supermarket assistant.
exercises.instructionUz: Xardi xonim va supermarket sotuvchisi o'rtasidagi dialogni to'g'ri so'zlar bilan to'ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
TANLOV: some/any, is/are, much/many

DIALOG (to'ldirilgan holda):
  H: I'd like SOME bread, please.
  A: Certainly. How MUCH would you like?
  H: Two loaves, please. ARE there ANY eggs?
  A: Of course. How MANY do you want?
  H: Six, please.

O'ZBEKCHA TARJIMASI:
  H: Menga non bering, iltimos.
  A: Albatta. Qancha xohlaysiz?
  H: Ikkita non, iltimos. Tuxum bormi?
  A: Albatta. Nechta xohlaysiz?
  H: Oltita, iltimos.

QOIDALAR:
  'bread' — SANALMAYDIGAN → SOME, HOW MUCH
  'eggs'  — SANALADIGAN KO'PLIK → ARE, HOW MANY
  MA'LUMOT savoli → ANY

H = Mrs Hardy (mijoz)
A = assistant (sotuvchi)

lines.whyUz:
TASDIQ gap ('I'd like') → SOME.
'bread' — SANALMAYDIGAN → 'a bread' XATO.

'eggs' — KO'PLIK → 'ARE there ...?'
MA'LUMOT savoli (taklif ham, iltimos ham emas) → ANY.

lines.textEn: Of course. How 5) ............ do you want?
lines.whyUz:
'eggs' — SANALADIGAN → HOW MANY.
2-band bilan solishtiring: bread → much, eggs → many.

exercises.instructionEn: Now, in pairs, have similar dialogues. Use words from the shopping list to replace the words in bold above.
exercises.instructionUz: Endi juftlikda shunga o'xshash dialoglar tuzing. Yuqoridagi qalin so'zlarni xarid ro'yxatidagi so'zlar bilan almashtiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  SA: I'd like some POTATOES, please.
  SB: Certainly. How MANY would you like?
  SA: TWO KILOS, please. Is there any WINE? etc

QOLIP:
  SA: I'd like some [mahsulot], please.
  SB: Certainly. How much/many would you like?
  SA: [miqdor], please. Is/Are there any [boshqa mahsulot]?

MUHIM — HAR SAFAR TEKSHIRING:
  Mahsulot SANALADIGANMI yoki YO'Q?
     sanaladigan (potatoes, eggs, sausages, bananas,
                  oranges, lettuces, pizzas)
        → How MANY,  ARE there any
     sanalmaydigan (bread, milk, wine, flour, salami)
        → How MUCH,  IS there any

XARID RO'YXATIDAGI MIQDORLAR:
  2 bottles of wine, 3 kilos of potatoes, 2 cartons of milk,
  12 slices of salami, 2 loaves of bread, 4 packets of flour,
  6 eggs, 2 lettuces, 12 sausages, 2 frozen pizzas,
  5 bananas, 6 oranges

items.question: I'd like some potatoes, please. — Certainly. How many would you like?
items.answer: Three kilos, please. Is there any wine?
items.whyUz:
Kitobda BERILGAN namuna.
'potatoes' — SANALADIGAN → HOW MANY.

items.question: I'd like some wine, please. — Certainly. How much would you like?
items.answer: Two bottles, please. Are there any eggs?
items.whyUz:
'wine' — SANALMAYDIGAN → HOW MUCH.
'eggs' — KO'PLIK → 'ARE there any ...?'

items.question: I'd like some milk, please. — Certainly. How much would you like?
items.answer: Two cartons, please. Are there any sausages?
items.whyUz:
'milk' — SANALMAYDIGAN → HOW MUCH.
'sausages' — KO'PLIK → ARE.

items.question: I'd like some salami, please. — Certainly. How much would you like?
items.answer: Twelve slices, please. Are there any bananas?
items.whyUz:
'salami' — SANALMAYDIGAN → HOW MUCH.
'slices' bilan sanaladi, lekin otning o'zi sanalmaydi.

items.question: I'd like some flour, please. — Certainly. How much would you like?
items.answer: Four packets, please. Is there any bread?
items.whyUz:
'flour' — SANALMAYDIGAN → HOW MUCH.
'bread' ham sanalmaydi → 'IS there any bread?'

items.question: I'd like some sausages, please. — Certainly. How many would you like?
items.answer: Twelve, please. Is there any milk?
items.whyUz:
'sausages' — SANALADIGAN → HOW MANY.
Miqdor so'zi kerak emas — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri son.

items.question: I'd like some oranges, please. — Certainly. How many would you like?
items.answer: Six, please. Are there any lettuces?
items.whyUz:
'oranges' — SANALADIGAN → HOW MANY.
'lettuces' — bu yerda bosh (dona) sifatida sanaladi.

items.question: I'd like some frozen pizzas, please. — Certainly. How many would you like?
items.answer: Two, please. Is there any flour?
items.whyUz:
'pizzas' — SANALADIGAN → HOW MANY.
'frozen' = muzlatilgan.

wordFormation.introUz: 33-bet — ijobiy va salbiy sifatlar hamda miqdor so'zlari.

groups.ruleUz: Restoran haqidagi IJOBIY va SALBIY sifatlar
groups.explanationUz: Reklama va mijozlar fikridagi qarama-qarshi juftliklar.
Ikki keng tarqalgan sifat yasovchi qo'shimcha.
Son 1 dan katta bo'lsa, MIQDOR so'zi ko'plikka o'tadi.

patterns.formula: There are many + sifat + ot + TO CHOOSE FROM.
patterns.exampleEn: There are many tasty pizzas and delicious pasta dishes to choose from.
patterns.exampleUz: Tanlash uchun ko'p mazali pitsalar va makaron taomlari bor.

patterns.formula: X is the PERFECT place TO + fe'l.
patterns.exampleEn: Luigi's is the perfect place to enjoy a meal with friends.
patterns.exampleUz: 'Luigi's' — do'stlar bilan ovqatlanish uchun mukammal joy.
patterns.explanationUz: 'the perfect place TO + fe'l' — reklama iborasi.

patterns.exampleEn: Make sure you book first because it is always very busy.
patterns.exampleUz: Avval stol band qilishga ishonch hosil qiling, chunki u doim juda gavjum.

patterns.exampleEn: 2 bottles of wine, 3 kilos of potatoes, 12 slices of salami
patterns.exampleUz: ikki shisha vino, uch kilo kartoshka, o'n ikki bo'lak salyami
patterns.explanationUz:
Son 1 dan katta → MIQDOR so'zi ko'plikda.
Ot esa o'zgarmaydi (sanalmaydigan bo'lsa).

patterns.formula: I'd like SOME + ot. — How much/many would you like? — miqdor, please.
patterns.exampleEn: I'd like some bread, please. — How much would you like? — Two loaves, please.
patterns.exampleUz: Menga non bering. — Qancha xohlaysiz? — Ikkita non, iltimos.

patterns.formula: IS there any + sanalmaydigan?  /  ARE there any + ko'plik?
patterns.exampleEn: Is there any wine? Are there any eggs?
patterns.explanationUz:
MA'LUMOT so'rash savolida ANY.
Fe'l otning turiga qarab tanlanadi.
